QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_7

question.text: Roshni Trust (education-for-disabled NPO) has the output: 'Braille textbooks distributed to visually impaired students.' As SIA, which combination of Indicator + MoV + Assumption is the MOST SMART and audit-ready for this output row in the LFM?

answer.text: Indicator: 'Many books given out'; MoV: 'Teachers will confirm'; Assumption: 'Project will work'
Indicator: 'Books'; MoV: 'Internal MIS only'; Assumption: 'Future is predictable'
Indicator: 'Books distributed'; MoV: 'Trust me'; Assumption: 'None needed'

Indicator: '10,000 Braille textbooks distributed to 2,500 students across 50 schools in Karnataka by 31 Dec 2025'; MoV: 'Distribution logs signed by school principals, cross-checked with independent beneficiary call-back survey of 10% sample'; Assumption: 'Schools remain operational; Braille printing vendor delivers on schedule'

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 4.2.3 (SMART) and 4.5 (LFM template), a sound output row needs: SPECIFIC numbers, MEASURABLE target, ACHIEVABLE scope, RELEVANT deliverable, TIME-BOUND deadline. Option B gives quantified distribution (10,000 books / 2,500 students / 50 schools / by 31 Dec 2025), dual-source MoV (signed logs + independent beneficiary call-back), and plausible external assumptions. A, C, D fail SMART and OVI basics. The Trap: A, C, B are all vague, non-SMART or lack OVI. They look like the kind of language that appears in poorly-drafted SE project docs — candidates must reject them as audit-ready. Cross-Exam Context: Application-style LFM construction is a staple of SAS engagement planning (XXIII Ch 7) and parallels CSR impact reporting under Section 135 (X-A Investment Adviser). Assessor's Pro-Tip: For every row you sign off on, mentally ask: 'If another SIA repeats my test using this MoV, will she get the same answer?' If yes, the row is assurance-grade; if not, flag it and request redesign.
